title: Absolute Noetherian approximation for qcqs algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$ and an inverse system $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with affine transitions, such that $Y\cong\varprojlim_iY_i$ and every $Y_i$ is quasi-separated and of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. Every $Y_i$ is Noetherian: it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and an etale scheme atlas is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. No Noetherian or finite type assumption is made on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate); Noetherian stages by spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04ZK (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian) over Spec Z, and finite type quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-splitting-filtration] to $Y$. We prove by descending induction that every $U_p$ has an affine inverse system of quasi-separated finite-type $\mathbf Z$-spaces as in the assertion, postponing the Noetherian clause to the end. Each $U_p$ is qcqs: quasi-compactness is in the filtration statement, and quasi-separatedness follows from [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence], which explicitly states that qc open subspaces of quasi-separated spaces are quasi-separated. For the base $p=n$, the filtration identifies $U_n$ with the qc separated scheme $V_n$. Apply [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] to this scheme. Use [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to replace the small cofiltered scheme system by a nonempty directed set. Its finite-type scheme stages are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and thus quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. If $Y$ is empty, the constant one-stage empty scheme system already suffices.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), first paragraph: filtration and schematic base of descending induction

proof.text: For the induction step put $X=U_p$, $U=U_{p+1}$, $V=V_p$, $Z=T_p$, and $f=f_p$. Thus $f:V\to X$ is surjective etale and is an isomorphism over the reduced closed complement $Z$ of $U$. The induction hypothesis gives $U=\varprojlim U_i$ with qcqs finite-type stages and affine transitions. Put $W=V\times_XU$, an open subscheme of $V$. By [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product], $W$ is qcqs. The map $W\to U$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], hence locally finitely presented; by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] it is also quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence finitely presented. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fp-over-space-limit-descent] to obtain $W_0\to U_0$ finitely presented with base change $W\to U$. Its source is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etaleness-eventual-stage] and replace $0$ by the resulting index, so that $W_0\to U_0$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), second and third paragraphs: the six hypotheses and descending W

proof.text: For $i\geq0$ set $W_i=W_0\times_{U_0}U_i$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] the maps $W_i\to U_i$ remain finitely presented, so their sources are qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]. Base change preserves etaleness by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Their transitions are affine and $W=\varprojlim W_i$ by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] and [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Since $W$ is a scheme, that latter node allows a further tail on which every $W_i$ is a scheme. The etale map $W_i\to U_i$ is locally of finite type. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], so is of finite type. Compose it with the finite-type map $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ using [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition]; the scheme agreement in [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] then makes $W_i$ a finite-type scheme over $\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-approximation-prescribed-open] to the qc separated scheme $V$ and the qc open $W\subset V$. Reindex the $U_i,W_i$ by its cofinal $\alpha$ and relabel the new index set as $I$. We obtain $V=\varprojlim V_i$, with $V_i$ finite-type schemes and affine transitions, and open subschemes $W_i\subset V_i$ preserved by inverse image. Cofinality preserves $U=\varprojlim U_i$: compatible cones extend uniquely using common upper bounds. All $V_i$ and $W_i$ are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), third and fourth paragraphs: schematic stages and prescribed-open scheme approximation

proof.text: Write $E_i=W_i\times_{U_i}W_i$. It is a scheme by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its projections are etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The diagonal $W_i\to E_i$ is etale: both its source and target are etale over $W_i$, so apply the cancellation clause of that same node. It is a monomorphism, hence an open immersion by [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to form the scheme $R_i=V_i\cup_{W_i}E_i$ along this diagonal and $W_i\subset V_i$. The two projections of $E_i$ and the identity on $V_i$ agree on $W_i$, so glue to maps $s_i,t_i:R_i\to V_i$. They are etale on the two open charts, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source]. The relation is the identity off $W_i$ and the kernel relation of $W_i\to U_i$ on $W_i$. More explicitly, its identity is the $V_i$ chart, inversion is identity on that chart and exchanges the factors of $E_i$, and composition on the open charts of composable pairs is the identity law if either arrow is in $V_i$, and $(a,b),(b,c)\mapsto(a,c)$ if both are in $E_i$. These maps agree on chart intersections. On each test scheme these formulas give a unique arrow for each related pair, reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity; local uniqueness on the charts gives the monomorphism $R_i\to V_i\times V_i$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), fourth paragraph: construction and etale equivalence-relation laws of R_i

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to set $X_i=V_i/R_i$. This is an algebraic space with surjective etale chart $V_i\to X_i$ and kernel pair $R_i$. It is quasi-compact since the chart map is continuous and surjective and $V_i$ is quasi-compact. The scheme $E_i$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product]; hence $R_i$, the union of two quasi-compact opens, is quasi-compact. Its maps to the quasi-separated scheme $V_i$ are quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. Now [lem-sfb-space-qs-atlas-criterion] gives quasi-separatedness of $X_i$. By [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], finite type of $V_i$ gives local finite type of $X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; together with quasi-compactness (or the same permanence node over the affine base), this makes $X_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), fourth paragraph: quotient stages and their finiteness

proof.text: The transition maps on $V_i$ and $E_i$ agree on $W_i$, so glue to $R_i\to R_j$ for $i\geq j$ and induce $X_i\to X_j$ by the quotient universal property in [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. Their identity and composition equations hold after the surjective charts $V_i$, hence hold on the quotients. The square $(R_i,V_i)\to(R_j,V_j)$ with the source projections is cartesian. Indeed, pull back the open cover $R_j=V_j\cup E_j$ along $V_i\to V_j$: the pieces are $V_i$ and $E_j\times_{s_j,V_j}V_i$, glued along $W_i$. Since $W_i=V_i\times_{V_j}W_j=W_j\times_{U_j}U_i$, the second piece is $E_i$. Its two projections are the prescribed ones. The two resulting chart isomorphisms agree on $W_i$, proving the asserted cartesian square. The same argument shows the inverse images in $R_i$ of the opens $V_j,E_j,W_j$ are exactly $V_i,E_i,W_i$.

The source-cartesian square gives $V_i\cong X_i\times_{X_j}V_j$ as follows, using the local lifting and kernel-pair clauses of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. A section of the right side is a class $x_i$ and a lift $v_j$ of its image. Etale locally lift $x_i$ to $v_i$. The equality in $X_j$ is etale locally an arrow $r_j$ joining the image of $v_i$ to $v_j$. The source-cartesian square gives a unique arrow $r_i$ with source $v_i$ over $r_j$; its target is the required lift over $v_j$. Two such lifts differ by an arrow over the identity arrow of $v_j$; source-cartesianness forces this arrow to be the identity. Thus the local lifts glue uniquely, proving the comparison is an isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], affineness of $V_i\to V_j$ now proves affineness of $X_i\to X_j$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], $X\prime=\varprojlim X_i$ exists and base change commutes with the limit. Fix a stage $0$. The cartesian squares identify $V=\varprojlim V_i$ with $X\prime\times_{X_0}V_0$, so $V\to X\prime$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Its kernel pair is $R=\varprojlim R_i$ by the same base-change formula, applied to $R_0=V_0\times_{X_0}V_0$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), cartesian quotient squares and the affine limit X prime

proof.text: The transitions $R_i\to R_j$ are affine: step 6 identifies them with base changes of $V_i\to V_j$, and [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] preserves affineness under base change. The scheme $R$ is obtained by gluing $V$ and $W\times_UW$ along $W$. To see the limit comparison on actual charts, fix stage $0$. The opens $V_0,E_0$ cover $R_0$; all later inverse images are $V_i,E_i$ by step 6. Base change of the limit along these two opens, using [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], therefore identifies their inverse images in $R$ with $\varprojlim V_i=V$ and $\varprojlim E_i=W\times_UW$. The latter identity follows directly from the universal property: compatible pairs in $W_i$ with equal images in every $U_i$ are exactly pairs in $W$ with equal images in $U$. Their intersection is $\varprojlim W_i=W$. These identifications preserve both projections to $V$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), last paragraph: identifying the limit relation chart by chart

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] to $f:V\to X$, giving its relation $V\times_XV$ and quotient $X$. The diagonal $V\to V\times_XV$ is an open immersion by the same cancellation and monomorphism argument of step 4, using [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open]. The other open is $W\times_UW$. These opens cover: a geometric pair not above $U$ lies above $Z$, and $V\times_XZ\to Z$ is an isomorphism, so the pair is diagonal. On their intersection the two components lie in $W$ and agree, hence the intersection is exactly $W$. This checks coverage on underlying point classes; both pieces are open subspaces, so it is a scheme open cover. Thus the gluing description of step 8 gives a unique isomorphism $R\cong V\times_XV$ preserving both projections. Apply [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] also to $V\to X\prime$: both $X$ and $X\prime$ are the same sheaf quotient $V/R$, hence are isomorphic. This completes the induction step and hence the construction for $Y=U_1$.

source.place: Tag 07SU (proposition-approximate), last paragraph: comparison with the original relation and completion of induction

proof.text: For every newly constructed stage $X_i$, the displayed atlas $V_i\to X_i$ is a scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $V_i$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian. The definition of locally Noetherian for spaces in the item asks for such an etale atlas, so $X_i$ is locally Noetherian. Step 5 already proves quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The schematic base case has the same Noetherian property by step 1. Thus every final $Y_i$ is Noetherian in the precise sense asserted. All index sets and reindexings are small in the fixed universes: the filtration is finite, and the scheme systems and prescribed-open refinement are small; no construction uses a proper-class index. None of the steps assumed $Y$ locally Noetherian or of finite type.

lean.statement: theorem exists_absoluteNoetherianApproximation (Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point Y.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated Y) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y ⟶ D), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk Y π)) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (h : i ≤ j), MapIsAffine (D.map (homOfLE h).op)) ∧ ∀ i : I, IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (D.obj (op i)) ∧ (∃ p : D.obj (op i) ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))))), MapIsFiniteType p) ∧ CompactSpace (Point (D.obj (op i)).obj.obj) ∧ ∃ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ (D.obj (op i)).obj.obj), IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian U.left
